_note: THE INPUT-ARM INVENTORY. One record per thing the original's interface responds to,
and one per thing OURS responds to that the original does not.
WHY IT EXISTS. docs/decisions.md C61: three screen groups were enumerated arm by arm
out of the decompilation and compared against our source, and we reproduced 80 of 185.
Every miss was a behaviour nobody had looked for, and three of them were inventions
rather than omissions. CLAUDE.md rule 5 came out of that measurement; this file is what
checks it, because a stated rule on this project does not hold and a checked one does.
THE CHECK, and it is the only thing everything else is arranged around:
the set of `id`s here with status "reproduced" is EQUAL, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, to the set
of `// arm: <id>` markers in the Rust. A record with no marker is a claim nobody kept; a
marker with no record is an arm nobody wrote down. crates/l2-game/tests/arms.rs is the
test and it names both differences.
THE MARKER. `// arm: 0xAAAAAAAA/slug` on its own line, immediately above or inside the
thing that implements it. The address is the ORIGINAL function the behaviour reproduces
-- not the painter of the screen it sits on -- and the slug disambiguates the several
arms one function can hold: FUN_0043BF07 alone is four of them. An id therefore starts
with `0x` and a marker is greppable as `// arm: 0x`.
STATUS, and there are five, because status is a CROSS-PRODUCT of two questions: what the
ORIGINAL has (live / dead / not at all) and what WE have (built it / did not). Five of the
six cells are named below; the sixth -- neither has it -- is not a record. They are one
field rather than two because these are the things anyone actually counts, and splitting
them would make every count a join for no gain in the common case.
reproduced -- we do it. MUST have exactly one marker.
missing    -- the original does it and we do not. The 1:1 gap.
dead       -- it is in the binary and cannot run. Not a gap: building it would be
reproducing code the shipped game never reaches. `why` says how that
was established, and it has to be an exhaustive check rather than a
failure to find.
invention  -- WE do it and the original does not. `removed` says whether it is still
in the tree. This is the direction C61 found three of and had no way to
count; an invention is worse than an omission because nothing looks
broken.
dead-reproduced -- we built an arm the shipped game cannot reach. Its own value, and
deliberately an awkward one, because it is a FINDING rather than a
category. It must not count in the 1:1 numerator, since no player can
reach it, and it must not hide inside `dead`, since we are carrying the
code. If one appears the likely right answer is to DELETE the code, not
to keep the record. MUST have exactly one marker, like anything we build.
So a marker is required exactly when we implement something: reproduced, invention or
dead-reproduced. `crates/l2-game/tests/arms.rs` holds that list in one place so the rule
cannot drift as statuses are added.
EVIDENCE is CLAUDE.md rule 4's: V verified against a second independent source, D a
straightforward reading of decompiled C, I inferred.
COUNTING. One (screen, gesture, guard) that a player can tell apart is one arm. A table
of N identical widgets hit-tested in one call is ONE arm (the menu bar's three titles,
the nine control-group keys); a ladder with N distinct outcomes is N arms (the overview
panel orders or looks: two). Where a count here differs from C61's, the counting rule is
the likeliest reason and the `group` totals in docs/battle.md section 15 say so.
COUNTED PER IMPLEMENTATION, NOT PER SCREEN. An arm live on three screens -- the overview
panel is -- is ONE record here, because the check compares this file against code and the
code has one function. docs/battle.md section 15.11 counts the same arms the other way,
once per screen, because that is how C61 counted and the two totals have to be
comparable: 33 records for 38 arms, and section 15.11 names the five that differ.
STATE OF THE FILE is in `groups` now, per group, as `complete`. A paragraph saying which
groups are finished goes stale silently; a flag the census can read does not.
GROUP is the unit somebody can claim COMPLETE -- an enumeration and its owner -- and not a
taxonomy of the interface. Any taxonomy is derivable from `screen`, so `group` carries the
thing that is not derivable: who enumerated this, and whether they finished. C61 measured
three groups, but those three were an artefact of how one evening happened to split across
three agents, which is the worst possible reason to freeze a taxonomy.

battlefield.note: Enumerated arm by arm from Screen_FrameInput, Screen_Draw and the window proc.

seam.what: 0x12 and 0x13, the prompt and the report either side of a battle
seam.note: 0x12 and 0x13 only. The rest of the campaign-side chrome is not in this file.

arms.what: Menu_OpenDropdown(&g_menuBarItems, 3) -- File, Options and Help are live during a battle, so a player can save, load, quit or open the options from the battlefield.
arms.note: The same arm is missing on the campaign map (crates/l2-game/src/screens/map.rs's table). Saving mid-battle is a question nobody has answered: Screen_HandleInput has no 0x29 arm and Menu_SaveGame does not test g_battlePhase.

arms.what: Ui_OkButtonClicked over the corner picture Ui_OkButton(0x1A8, 0x1A6) drew -- a 24x24 box tested on the LEFT button's RELEASE -- closes the screen back to the campaign map.
A right release goes back to 0x29. It does NOT undo the box -- the live selection is left exactly as the last pointer motion made it, because the cancel is a screen change and nothing else.

Screen_HandleInput's 0x1A arm, when the widget test declines and g_diploKind is 1..4, sets DAT_005AEB78 = 1 and calls FUN_0040210C(g_diploLetterDraft + (kind - 1) * 200, 199). FUN_0040210C is a bounded copy OUT OF DAT_005CD550, the game's one shared text-edit buffer that FUN_00401D26(ch) inserts typed characters into at cursor DAT_005BB4A8 -- so the four 200-byte buffers at 0x0053F2B8 are snapshots harvested from a single editor once a frame, not four independent fields. Diplo_OpenCompliment and its three siblings run the copy the other way (FUN_00402009) when the dialog opens, and Diplo_SendClicked copies the finished one into g_diploLetter + localPlayer * 0xCA, which is saved with the game and drawn to the recipient by Msg_DrawWindow.
arms.note: Not built here: text entry is a separate branch's. ComposeScreen carries the draft as a String so that branch has somewhere to write, and the send already copies it. The `what` above was corrected after the decompilation corpus was rebuilt with 211 more names: the first reading called FUN_0040210C 'the keyboard entry field', which is the harvest rather than the entry.

arms.what: The 0x1A arm's right release: g_screenId = 0, the campaign map -- NOT back to 0x0B. Tested after the county picker, so a right click over the map still leaves.
g_screenId = 0x29; DAT_0053F238 = 0; DAT_0053E9AC = 1.
arms.why: See 0x00432221/dead-0x28-edge-scroll. Note it would UNPAUSE the battle, which is the only place other than the pause button that writes DAT_0053F238 to zero -- so whatever 0x28 was, leaving it started the fighting.

arms.what: Screen_FrameInput's 0x0B arm: a right release sets g_screenId = 0 without consulting the corner button at all. Right-click exits -- the gesture docs/agents.md records this project as systematically missing.
0x13 has a right-button test and an OK-corner test, either of which returns to the map. 0x12, one screen earlier, has NEITHER -- which is what made right-click-to-Decline look reasonable.

`if (g_battleHoverOnField == 0) g_screenId = 0x29` -- the pointer leaving the viewport ends the drag. Tested AFTER the two selection guards, so a release on the very frame the pointer leaves still commits.

The whole of Screen_FrameInput's 0x12 arm: the multiplayer sync latch DAT_00553FC8, and FUN_004BBEA7, a 20- or 30-second answer timeout. Both call Battle_Decline. FUN_004BBEA7 returns 0 unconditionally when g_multiplayer is clear, so IN SINGLE PLAYER THE ARM DOES NOTHING AT ALL and the prompt waits for ever.
arms.note: Missing because we have no multiplayer, not because it was overlooked. The waiting-for-ever half is reproduced and is correct.

arms.what: A right release sets DAT_00568470 = 0x1389 -- 5001, one past the limit Battle_CheckOutcome counts it up to -- so it SKIPS the outcome banner rather than dismissing it. The whole of 0x2B's arm.
The pointer on the outermost pixel of the screen scrolls the battle camera ONE cell, against the campaign map's two rows and one column. Map_ScrollStep's g_battlePhase == 2 half.
Screen_FrameInput's 0x28 arm opens with Map_EdgeScroll().
arms.why: Screen 0x28 is unreachable. Every immediate write of g_screenId in Lords2.exe was enumerated -- 212 `mov byte ptr [0x004EAC50], imm8` sites, values 0x00..0x45 -- and 0x28 is absent while 0x29, 0x2A and 0x2B are present; no decompiled function assigns it, and the indirect writes (g_screenIdSaved, g_menuPrevScreen) can only restore a value g_screenId already held.

arms.what: BattleMap_Click: the 160x160 panel at (480, 24), two pixels a cell over the whole 80x80 field. Left button with a selection, no oil selected and unpaused ORDERS to that cell; anything else, the right button included, puts the camera there. Reached from Screen_FrameInput's EPILOGUE, so it is live on 0x29, 0x2A and 0x2B alike.
Hotspot_Test(0x1E0, 0x1C0, &DAT_004DC710, 5) -- the five 32x32 buttons in a row at (480, 448). This record is the hit test; the five actions are five records of their own.

The six g_diploWidgets handlers -- Diplo_OpenGift 0x00436141, OpenCompliment 0x0043618B, OpenInsult 0x004361DA, OpenAlliance 0x00436229, OpenAskHelp 0x004362CA, OpenAskAttack 0x0043631E. One record because they differ only in the g_diploKind they set and the draft buffer they clear. Diplo_OpenAlliance is the one with a decision in it: it picks kind 4 over kind 3 exactly when the target is already this realm's ally, so ONE widget serves group 72 rows 5 and 6.

The gift dialog's plus and minus at (184, 240) and (216, 240), hotspots 1 and 0 of one handler: ten crowns a click, clamped to [0, my gold] on EVERY click -- so an amount already set follows the treasury down when something else spends it.

The same handler's hotspot 0, the cross, and it is the function's first statement: g_screenId = 0x0B, back to the lord cards. It lands somewhere DIFFERENT from the corner button and the right release on the same screen, both of which go to the campaign map.

Diplo_SendClicked hotspot 1, the tick. It closes the screen and copies the draft into the player's g_diploLetter slot BEFORE it validates, so all six of its refusals -- L2.eng 240, 241, 242, 243, 244 and 219 -- are messages on the map rather than a red light on the dialog. Then Diplo_Post, or net command 0x48/0x49 in multiplayer.

Diplo_PayHelpClicked -- the accept button on the category-10 message window an ally raises when it answers a help or attack request with Pay -. It calls Diplo_PayForHelp(myAlly, me, g_diploHelpCounty, g_diploHelpPrice), which moves the gold, increments the multiple and points the ally's targetCounty at the county.
arms.note: The RULE is built -- l2_kingdom::diplomacy::pay_for_help, with the price and county on Kingdom::diplomacy -- and the PROMPT is not: Msg_DrawWindow is 10,915 bytes and only its text and voice lookups have ever been read, so there is no window on screen to click. This and 0x00436872 are the only two places a person answers a lord rather than writing to one, and both are unreachable.

arms.what: The Accept alliance ? prompt's two buttons (L2.eng group 180, message category 0x0B). Hotspot 1 calls Diplo_FormAlliance(g_localPlayer, DAT_0057C8B8) -- and DAT_0057C8B8 is not a diplomacy global: Msg_DrawWindow writes it to whichever realm's letter is currently on screen, beside its portrait and name, so for this prompt it is the offering lord. Hotspot 0 declines. Note the guard is (offerer is human) || (hotspot != 0), so declining an AI's offer in single player runs NOTHING at all -- not even a refusal message. The offer simply lapses when the offering realm clears offerPending at the top of its next turn.
arms.note: Blocked on the same unread Msg_DrawWindow as 0x004367FF.

arms.what: Diplo_PickLordCard walks the same rivals the painter stacked and hit-tests each 82x78 card at (0x30, slot*100 + 0x31); the first hit becomes g_diploTarget. It runs AFTER the widget test, and the two can never both hit because the cards end at x = 130 and the menu starts at x = 400.

Diplo_PickCountyFromMap(0x60, 0xB0) -- the 128x128 county raster on the ask-for-help and ask-for-attack dialogs, indexed straight out of g_minimapCounty. Guarded by g_diploKind >= 5, and a pixel whose county is 0 is NOT a hit, so a click on the sea inside the map falls through to the corner button behind it.
PAUSE. Toggles DAT_0053F238 with a bitwise NOT, so it flips between 0 and -1. Battle_Start seeds it to 0xFFFFFFFF, so A BATTLE STARTS PAUSED and the first thing a player does is press this.

RETREAT -- Ui_OpenConfirm(12) 'Retreat from field?', or Ui_OpenConfirm(11) 'Surrender castle?' when this is a siege and the local player owns army B. Both callbacks reach FUN_0043BE65, which is Battle_AutoResolve and the return to the campaign. Guarded on g_battleChoiceOwner == 1.

Siege only, garrison only, castle level 3 or more, once per battle: FUN_00496B9F clears a 7x4 patch of cells flagged 0x40, writes surface 3 over it, adds 4 to both siege scores and rebuilds the pathfinding. On a field battle it enqueues message 0x6E and does nothing else.
arms.note: The BUTTON and its four guards are reproduced; FUN_00496B9F's rules are the siege agent's and are stubbed to the once-per-battle latch.

arms.what: CHARGE -- FUN_0047A76D puts every one of the local player's figures of troop type under 7 into free pursuit and halts its unit, which switches the every-500-frame reform off. Guarded by DAT_0055322C, so it fires ONCE in a battle.
arms.note: Not Order_ChargeNearest (0x0048C8AF), which is the AI's and also clears the withdraw flag and the figures' targets.

arms.what: Ui_OpenConfirm(9) 'Autocalc battle?'. Yes runs FUN_0043BE65 -- Battle_AutoResolve, which reads the CAMPAIGN records and never Battle_WriteBackCasualties, so every man killed so far is unkilled and the result is computed from the armies as they walked on.
A left press inside the viewport records the anchor cell and the anchor pixel and takes the screen to 0x2A. Gated on DAT_00568964 == 1 (input armed by Battle_Start) and g_battleHoverOnField.

The release, classified by FUN_00479CF7 into three: moved 25 pixels or more on either axis is a BOX and commits with FUN_0043C247(player, 1, ...); barely moved over one of your own men NUDGES THE BOX OUT BY EIGHT PIXELS each way and commits that, so a click picks a 16-pixel square; barely moved over nothing DOES NOTHING AT ALL and in particular does not clear the selection. The commit runs FUN_00478987, which allocates a new unit when the selection is not exactly one whole unit -- so a box drawn round half a unit SPLITS it.

The release test is `(g_mouseLeftReleased || g_mouseLeftDoubleClick) && g_screenId == 0x2A`, so a double click commits an open box exactly as a release would. Not a verb of its own: Windows sends WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK INSTEAD OF the second WM_LBUTTONDOWN, so without this the second click of a fast double click would leave the drag open with no press to end it.
arms.note: This is the second reader of g_mouseLeftDoubleClick that C61 predicted and crates/l2-game/src/input.rs denied. Hotspot_Test's kind-2 widgets are a third reader and are not an arm.

arms.what: While the button is down and the pointer has moved, FUN_0043C247(player, 0, ...) clears and re-boxes the selection LIVE. The 0 is what stops it regrouping units on every pointer motion.

A left press on one of the banners in the right column DROPS that figure from the selection (FUN_0043C4C6) -- it does not select it. The layout is one of three from DAT_004D31F4 by how many you hold, and only the first FIFTY are clickable whichever layout is up.

A right release CLEARS THE WHOLE SELECTION (FUN_0043C55C). Refused inside the overview panel -- x >= 0x1E1 && 0x18 <= y <= 0xB7 -- and note the off-by-one: the panel starts at 0x1E0, so its leftmost column deselects.
arms.note: This is the arm the project's 'right click exits' habit would have replaced with a way out of the battle. C61's second pattern.

arms.what: A left release on ground that holds none of your own men, with something selected and the battle unpaused, is an order: FUN_0043C634 plays a troop cry and calls BattleUnit_Order(currentUnit, cell, hoverEnemy, hoverWoodland, 0).

0x2A's ladder runs FUN_0043C57D as its second guard, so the order arm is live during a drag as well as on the field. In practice FUN_0043BF07 consumes the release first and this never fires; it is recorded because a change to the order of the two would make it fire, and because 'the same function on a second screen' is exactly what C61 found nobody counts.

H and V re-issue the player's current unit an order AT ITS OWN POSITION with BattleUnit_Order's sixth argument set to 1 or 2, which stores 0 or 1 in unit +0x09. Formation_ComputeRect (0x0048A1C9) reads that byte in one line -- `if (field_0x9 == 1) g_formationCols = 2` -- so the two keys are LINE and COLUMN and nothing else touches the byte.
arms.note: Settles docs/battle.md section 1's 'unnamed and untraced' for unit +0x09.

arms.what: Ctrl and 1..9 store the current selection into DAT_00553400 + (key - '1') * 0x18. The window procedure latches VK_CONTROL into DAT_004DF3A8 and its digit arm calls a DIFFERENT FUNCTION depending on it.

Keys 1..9 recall a stored selection and PUT THE CAMERA ON IT -- the function ends by scanning for the first selected figure and setting the viewport corner seven cells above and left of it. Nine slots (VK 0x31..0x39); Battle_Start clears ten.

The first thing Screen_FrameInput does on EVERY screen: a right release inside a 48x48 box round the message scroll dismisses it and SWALLOWS THE CLICK, so it never reaches the screen's own arms. A battle can raise messages (the siege gate button enqueues three of them), so this is reachable here.
arms.note: Not the battlefield's own arm -- it is every screen's, and is recorded under this group because a battle is where it was noticed.

arms.what: Battle_CheckOutcome and FUN_004782C5 both count DAT_00568470 up once a frame; past 5000 the banner gives way to Battle_WriteBackCasualties and Battle_ReturnToCampaign(1). Not an input arm; recorded because the skip above is one and is meaningless without it.

Battle_UpdateHover recomputes the five hover globals every frame: on-field, the cell, its surface, whether it is woodland, and whether the occupant is a friend, a picked friend or an enemy. Two of the three order arms read nothing else.
arms.note: One clause is reproduced CORRECTED rather than as found -- see docs/bugs.md B69, the stale figure index.

arms.what: F4 adds one hit to figures 1..20. A cheat, gated on DAT_0053F684 == 1.
The left and right arrow keys step g_debugSelectedMan down and up through 0..80, which is the figure the debug panel prints. UNGATED -- the only one of the four that is.

F2 cycles DAT_00568960 through 0, 1, 2, which picks between BattleDebug_Panel and two other overlays. All three draw only when DAT_0055402C is set, which is F3, which is gated on the debug flag DAT_0053F684 -- so the developers' panel is off in a shipped game and F2 alone cannot turn it on.
F3 toggles DAT_0055402C, which is what makes the three battle overlays draw at all. Gated on DAT_0053F684 == 1.

Battle_Frame's cursor ladder for 0x28..0x2A: seven leaves over four cursor kinds -- 0 arrow, 4 move, 5 attack, 6 select. An enemy under the pointer beats everything; 0x2A is always the arrow; with a selection in hand a pointer OUTSIDE the field still shows the move cursor as long as it is above y 184, which is the overview panel, where a click really does order.

DAT_004DDBB0[1], the thumb down at (372, 116), hotspot id 0 -> Battle_Decline, which is Battle_AutoResolve and the report. The table holds exactly these two records: g_sliderWidgets begins 48 bytes on at 0x004DDBE0, and the count DAT_00554408 is 2 when g_battleChoiceOwner == 1 and 0 otherwise.
DAT_004DDBB0[0], the thumb up at (332, 116), hotspot id 1 -> FUN_0043B593 -> Battle_Start. It RAISES THE BATTLEFIELD; it does not settle the battle.
When the local player did not own the choice, any click, right-click or key settled the battle by the standing policy.
arms.why: Battle_ChooseSettlement writes a widget count of 0 for a bystander, so the prompt has no widgets and no exit but the multiplayer timeout. In a single-player game the state cannot arise at all.

arms.what: Enter took the field.
arms.why: As above. The window procedure's Enter arm is FUN_0043600C, a text-field commit.

arms.what: Escape declined the battle.
arms.why: No key reaches screen 0x12 in the original. The window procedure's Escape arm calls Menu_Quit or sets DAT_005AEB68 = 1 and never touches the prompt.

arms.what: A right release on the take-the-field prompt ran Battle_Decline. Screen 0x12's arm has no right-button test of any kind.
arms.why: 'Right click exits' generalised from the screens where it is true. C61 found it by enumeration and this is its removal.

arms.what: Escape and Enter dismissed the battle report.
arms.why: 0x13's arm is a right-button test and Ui_OkButtonClicked. No key.
